slot.brief: Uniformly charged sphere or long straight charged wire; find the electric field at a given outside distance by constructing a Gaussian surface and substituting into Gauss's law.

stem: A long straight wire carries a uniform charge per unit length of $5.56\times10^{-9}$ C m$^{-1}$. Find the electric field at a distance of $0.10$ m from it. Take $\varepsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$ N$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: For a long straight wire, E = λ/(2πε₀r) = (5.56×10⁻⁹)/(2π×8.85×10⁻¹²×0.10) ≈ 1000 N C⁻¹.

working:
For a cylindrical Gaussian surface, $E(2\pi rL)=\lambda L/\varepsilon_0$; hence $E=\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0r}=\dfrac{5.56\times10^{-9}}{2\pi(8.85\times10^{-12})(0.10)}\approx1000$ N C$^{-1}$.

Independent check: For a long straight wire, E = λ/(2πε₀r) = (5.56×10⁻⁹)/(2π×8.85×10⁻¹²×0.10) ≈ 1000 N C⁻¹.
solution:
By Gauss’s law for a long straight charged wire,
$$E=\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}=\frac{5.56\times10^{-9}}{2\pi(8.85\times10^{-12})(0.10)}\approx 1000\ \text{N C}^{-1}.$$
